evaluations.title: Exact Rational and Algebraic Expansion of the Ariadne 494-Vector Scaffold
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Ariadne 494-vector fixed scaffold (Archive #14 / Eval 499) for absolute exact capacity. Bypasses the 30-support restriction by testing a massive, unfiltered exact rational and Q(sqrt(2)) alphabet for exact combinatorial replacements via MILP, attempting to reach N>=597.

evaluations.title: Chart-conditioned witness generation around the N600 role swap
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the known standard/faulted role swap of the exact N=600 code changes chart-native witness generation. The evaluation must recover the known neutral held-out rows as a positive control, then compare nearby chart-conditioned generators for non-duplicate candidate families or improved blocker profiles. This is not a broad local atlas or N=601 search.

evaluations.title: Exact Algebraic Subtractive Co-Design: 1-for-2 Replacement via Polynomial Intersection
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Instead of searching a pre-generated grid, this experiment deletes one specific rattler from the N=600 macroscopic fault and attempts to insert TWO vectors by solving the exact multivariate polynomial system representing their tight contacts with the 599-vector frozen core.

evaluations.title: Three-split blocker topology and exchange map
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Compare Ariadne 494+104, Archive #5 495+103, and Archive #6 496+104 configurations by covering radius, blocker topology, and exact tight-row/filler exchange potential, to identify whether Ariadne's filler cloud can trade slack for archived tight rows.

evaluations.title: Rigidity spectrum of the d=11 N=600 record + cross-dimensional cold-reachability calibration (d=4/8/11)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Anchor computation for the reachability-vs-rigidity question. Two deliverables. (1) The infinitesimal-rigidity spectrum of the certified d=11 N=600 record as a spherical contact framework: build the exact contact graph (pairs at inner product exactly 1/2), form the spherical rigidity matrix, and report its rank, the dimension of the trivial rotation space SO(11), the count of nontrivial infinitesimal flexes, and the number of self-stresses (isostatic vs over-constrained). (2) A cold-start continuous-packing reachability calibration in d=4 (target 24), d=8 (target 240, E8), and d=11 (target 600): from random initializations, does first-order repulsion reach the known optimum/record, or jam short? The pairing tests whether

evaluations.title: Sweeping Fractional Circumcenter Diagnostic
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps all 102 messy points to compute the exact geometric centers of their local voids (bounded by core dots > 1.95). Verifies if these exact centers are globally valid kissing points.

evaluations.title: Polynomial Ideals of the Top N=601 Continuous Near-Misses
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact active constraint sets from the best numerical N=601 continuous near-misses and formulates them as systems of polynomial equations in SymPy to test their exact solvability over the reals.

evaluations.title: Balanced-coordinate-replication cores: does breaking the 8+3 split lower covering radius f*?
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #528 showed the d=11 record's covering radius f*=1/sqrt(3) is realized by 64 body-diagonal deep holes on 8 of 11 coordinates (an (8_3) incidence config); coords {6,9,10} host no deep hole, matching the uneven coordinate replication (12 vs 8, Eval #220). Archive #16/Eval #527 shows f* is config-dependent (0.5073 for a 494+104 N=598). CORE BET: build D11 norm-4 cores with BALANCED coordinate replication across all 11 coords, add rattlers via fixed-core chamber packing, and test whether covering radius drops below 1/sqrt(3). This is a construction probe (spine), with two reusable byproducts: (i) an exact certificate of the record's (8_3) deep-hole

evaluations.title: Rigidity/self-stress signature as a basin discriminator: can it separate the N=600 record from known-different exact D11 configs?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Central positive-instrument test for the reachability/rigidity lane. Eval #533 gave the exact rigidity spectrum of the N=600 record (hyperstatic 496-contacted skeleton + 104 contact-isolated rattlers). This experiment asks whether a BASIS-INDEPENDENT rigidity/self-stress signature can serve as a basin discriminator: does it cluster genuine same-basin continuous perturbations of the record together, while separating them from genuinely DIFFERENT known exact configs at the same frontier — Ariadne's 494+104 N=598 chamber (Eval #522, distinct filler cloud that blocks the record axis) and Archive #5's 495+103 N=598 (Eval #247)? Deliverable: a normalized signature (self-stress density, sorted equilibrium-stress spectrum, contacted-subframework rank index, contact-degree histogram) and

evaluations.title: Equal-effort cold-reachability control (d=4/8/11): is the #533 cold-search failure genuine or under-optimization?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Calibration control resolving the #533 confound. In Eval #533 cold pure-packing failed to reach the known optimum in ALL of d=4 (24), d=8 (240), d=11 (600) at 0/5 seeds, but the d=4/d=8 runs used a shorter step budget (117 vs 260 steps/stage) and d=4 reached max IP 0.517 (near 0.5), so the failures may be under-optimization rather than a genuine reachability barrier. This experiment equalizes optimization effort across dimensions (same per-N-scaled but generous step budget, more seeds, best-of restarts) and reports whether cold first-order search reaches the 60-degree threshold in each dimension. It isolates whether cold-search reachability is dimension/structure-dependent (a

evaluations.title: Resource-exchange active-template compiler v1
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Build a first reusable compiler for pre-coordinate slack-tight exchange motifs. The evaluation should use Archive #16's 494+104 contrast chamber and the Archive #6 N600 record only as calibration objects, then construct and test active templates for regenerating a filler cluster with a blocked tight row present. Success is not a score improvement; success is a saved motif library and layer-classified outcomes that distinguish rank/PSD, anchor-interface, numerical-coordinate, and exactification/margin failures.

evaluations.title: Exact Polyhedral Chebyshev Center of the N=600 Rattler Voids
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact geometric capacity of individual rattler voids in the N=600 macroscopic fault by computing the exact Chebyshev center of the active polyhedral cone defined by the frozen core, testing whether the exact void radius natively admits an insertion.

evaluations.title: Simplex-like Walk on Exact Algebraic Branches of N=600 Voids
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a simplex-like pivoting algorithm on the exact algebraic boundary of a deleted rattler void. Starts from the Chebyshev center, exactifies the nearest 10 active constraints into a polynomial system, solves for the real roots, and iteratively swaps violated constraints to walk the 1D exact algebraic branches (rank-9 systems) in search of a fully valid insertion point.

evaluations.title: M1: soft stiffness-spectrum (instrument B) validation — tolerance-robust, N-controlled basin discriminator?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Decisive validation of instrument B for the rigidity/reachability lane. Instrument A (hard-contact rigidity signature, Evals #533/#537) is well-defined only on exact certified configs and is brittle at jamming under contact tolerance. Instrument B is the SOFT stiffness / dynamical-matrix spectrum: continuous in configuration, computable on numerical near-misses, standard in jamming physics. B is the forward-utility pre-screen candidate but is untested. This experiment runs three sub-tests with pre-registered kill/validate outcomes: (a) correctness gate — random O(11) rotation + relabeling of the record must give B-distance ~0; (b) within-basin stability — B across convergence snapshots of the record (max-IP 0.5001 -> 0.5000001)

evaluations.title: Exact Algebraic Ideal of the 496-Core Deep Holes (Covering Radius)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact polynomial ideal of the deepest numerical voids in the frozen 496-vector small-norm core of the N=600 fault. Determines if the continuous stall at 1/sqrt(3) is an exact algebraic reality and whether any real algebraic branches escape it.

evaluations.title: Active-Set Algebraic Exactification Algorithm
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Active-Set Projection algorithm to extract the algebraic null-space and minimal fields of the 67 off-center rattlers from the baseline configuration.

evaluations.title: Maximal Independent Set of the 496-Core Continuous Deep Holes
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact deep holes of the 496-vector N=600 fault core. Since Eval 543 proved the single-vector covering radius is ~0.288 (well below 0.5), this experiment searches for an independent set of >= 105 mutually compatible deep holes to natively surpass the 104-rattler limit.

evaluations.title: M1-fix: clean instrument-B validation (full low-eigen solve + tiny-feasible-only within-basin perturbations)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #542 returned KILL for the soft stiffness-spectrum instrument B (within-basin band 0.3 == N-controlled cross-config distance 0.3), but the coder flagged the run as only partially faithful: it used a Ritz-compressed spectrum instead of a full sparse low-eigenvalue solve, and the within-basin 'noisy target 0.5001' was a relaxation SNAPSHOT with structural noise rather than the specified tiny feasible perturbation — both of which would inflate the within-basin band and could manufacture a false KILL; distances also appear bin-quantized (metric too coarse). This is the single sanctioned implementation-fix: rerun the B-validation with (i) a genuine full sparse low-eigenvalue solve of

evaluations.title: Mapping the Exact Algebraic Boundary of Rattler Voids (Groebner/SymPy)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Since the 104 rattlers in N=600 are floating loosely (contact degree 0), their voids are not saturated by them. This experiment uses exact polynomial intersection to find the true tight boundaries of these voids. It identifies the top 10 closest core vectors to a rattler and solves the exact algebraic intersection to find boundary vertices.

evaluations.title: Exact 1D Algebraic Branch Mapping of the N=600 Rattler Voids (Rank-9 Systems)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Drops one constraint from the exact tangent roots of the N=600 rattler voids to form exact rank-9 polynomial systems. Sweeps the resulting 1D algebraic curves (circles) to test if they contain any contiguous feasible arcs that can host multiple exact additions.

evaluations.title: Exact Two-Vector Insertion on Rank-9 Algebraic Branches (N=601 Target)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 548, we identified 4 rank-9 algebraic branches (1D circles) inside the 496-core voids that possess sufficient radius and feasible arc length to natively host two vectors. This experiment exactly constructs the optimal two points on these branches and tests them against the full 599-vector frozen configuration to attempt an exact N=601 certification.

evaluations.title: S2 lever selection: decomposed f_core measurement + support-pair-incidence across three cores
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Pre-commit S2 (approved proposal). By monotonicity of the covering radius f(C)=min_u max_i <u,c_i> in the point set (f_full >= f_core), the norm-4 CORE sets the lower floor for any config's covering radius; rattlers only raise it. This eval measures f_core (core alone) for three cores — the record (~496), Ariadne Eval #522 (494), and one balanced core — via full sphere min-max, attributes each deepest hole's active contacts (axis / weight-4 overlap m), and reports the support-pair-incidence histogram. It tests the coverage-law prediction that the record floors at 1/sqrt(3) because its 30-support system is a near-covering design on coordinate pairs

evaluations.title: M2: active-set/SQP boundary solver vs cold first-order — creating a reachable/unreachable contrast (d=4/8/11)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: The reachability axis currently has NO positive class: cold first-order search reached the optimum in none of d=4 (24), d=8 (240, E8), d=11 (600) even at equal effort (#538). Ariadne's guidance and my lane require a reachable/unreachable CONTRAST to test whether a rigidity/stiffness invariant predicts the successful solver class. This experiment builds an ACTIVE-SET / SQP boundary solver — the class that lands ON active constraints rather than pooling short of them — and tests from-scratch reachability of the known optima in d=4/8/11, comparing directly against the cold first-order baseline. Expected discriminator: active-set may reach the low-frustration optima (d=4, E8,

evaluations.title: Elastic partial-Gram patch benchmark v2
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Implement the first explicit schema and benchmark for elastic partial-Gram exchange patches. The evaluation should validate the patch interface on synthetic controls, then perform a small D11 calibration comparing fixed-boundary and elastic-boundary versions of the Archive #16 blocked-axis motif. Success is an operational schema, controlled feasibility diagnostics, and layer-classified outcomes, not a score improvement.

evaluations.title: Generative Discriminant Alphabet: Extracting Real Roots of the Ariadne 494-Scaffold
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Uses the active-constraint polynomial formulation generatively rather than retrospectively. Samples 100,000 localized rank-10 constraint subsets from the exact Ariadne 494-scaffold, exactifies them into SymPy polynomial ideals, and extracts all real algebraic roots (positive and zero discriminant). Constructs an exact conflict graph of this newly generated algebraic alphabet and solves for maximum independent set to find N >= 598.

evaluations.title: Instrument Calibration: Active Contact Rank of Ariadne Fillers
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Retrospective calibration of the rank-10 tangent generator against the known Ariadne fillers. Measures the exact active contact rank and filler-filler coupling of the known successful N=596/598 configuration to determine if the tangency assumption holds.

evaluations.title: Subtractive Co-Design: Geometric Capacity of Rank-9 Branch Circles
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Measures the exact circle radius of all rank-9 algebraic branches around the N=600 rattlers. If the radius squared is < 0.25, it is geometrically impossible to fit two valid points on the branch, proving that 1D branch 1-for-2 substitutions are unconditionally impossible regardless of blocker deletion.

evaluations.title: Generative Algebraic Dictionary via Voronoi Indexing
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Uses massive numerical sampling against the 492-core to identify unique topological voids (active sets). Exactifies these sets algebraically to build a dictionary of novel exact candidate points.

evaluations.title: Subtractive Co-Design: Minimal Blocker Sets on Rank-9 Branches
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Scans the high-capacity rank-9 branches of the N=600 configuration, samples mutually valid pairs, and identifies the minimal background blocker set. Deletes the blockers to execute a 2-for-2 or 1-for-2 algebraic swap.

evaluations.title: Geometric Capacity of Rank-8 Spheres (1-for-3 Potential)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Measures the intrinsic geometric capacity of rank-8 algebraic spheres around the N=600 rattlers to determine if they can host three mutually compatible points (a necessary condition for a 1-for-3 swap).

evaluations.title: M1: does rigidity/stiffness fingerprint distance predict warm-continuation compatibility, beating a shared-row/contact-count baseline?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: First committed experiment of the approved lane (Tick 273-335). Tests whether structural fingerprint distance (soft stiffness spectrum B / exact rigidity signature A) predicts WARM continuation compatibility between a seed and a target, and — critically — whether it beats a trivial baseline (shared-exact-row fraction + contact-count difference). Corpus of configs with KNOWN continuation outcomes: record N=600, Ariadne-522 (494+104, reached by continuation to a branch that BLOCKS the record axis), Archive5-247 (495+103), plus my near-miss artifacts (#468/#481, MILP-glued, failed to reach record) and cross-substrate seeds (K12 section, symmetric #461). For each seed->target pair, run a bounded warm active-set continuation to

evaluations.title: Subtractive Co-Design: Steerable 2-Point Insertion on Rank-8 Spheres
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Measures the minimal background blocker set for 1-for-2 substitutions on 2D Rank-8 algebraic spheres. Tests whether the extra degree of freedom allows steering around the core constraints that blocked the 1D Rank-9 branches.

evaluations.title: M2: does the stiffness fingerprint predict continuation destiny where row-overlap is BLIND (numerical near-misses; same-scaffold different-branch)?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: M1 (#559) found fingerprint B separates CONTINUES from FAILS perfectly (AUC 1.0) but so does the trivial row-overlap baseline (AUC 1.0, larger margin) — B is REDUNDANT on M1's bimodal corpus (configs share either ~490+ exact rows or ~none). B can only earn non-redundancy where row-overlap is uninformative. M2 tests exactly those regimes: (i) GENUINE numerical near-misses with ~0 exact rows to any target (row-overlap baseline blind by construction) — does B predict which target the near-miss warm-continues to? and (ii) SAME-SCAFFOLD DIFFERENT-BRANCH pairs (Ariadne-522 shares 494 rows with the record = high overlap but continues to a different branch

evaluations.title: Coupled Algebraic Varieties: Intrinsic Compatibility of Adjacent Branches
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Measures the intrinsic algebraic compatibility of neighboring Rank-9 branches. Formulates the exact coupled polynomial ideal to determine if adjacent branches overlap everywhere (minimum mutual dot > 0.5) or if a solvable joint branch network exists.

evaluations.title: Protected-hole substrate design: largest valid norm-4 vs mixed-4/6 core keeping a target hole addable
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Turning the proved coverage law into a source law. For a body-diagonal hole H on support S, coverage by an integer row of squared norm n with sign-matched overlap m is m*(coeff)/(sqrt t sqrt n). To keep H addable (coverage <= 1/2), protection constraints exclude axes on S, norm-4 rows with overlap m>=2 on S, and norm-6 rows with overlap m=3 on S (norm-6 m<=2 gives 0.471 <= 1/2). This eval computes the LARGEST valid substrate (pairwise IP <= 1/2) satisfying protection, for one target triple and one 4-subset, comparing norm-4-only vs mixed norm-4/norm-6 candidate universes, via exact MIS/greedy. Output

evaluations.title: Elastic patch schema and control hardening
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Harden the elastic partial-Gram patch schema and synthetic controls from Eval #552. This evaluation should implement stricter validation semantics, invalid-example coverage, explicit pass/fail criteria for feasible/rank-pressure/boundary-elastic/collapse controls, and reusable artifacts for future patch evaluations. It should not perform new D11 search beyond optional smoke loading.

evaluations.title: Coupled Branch Network: 3-for-4 Swap on the (508, 499, 510) Rattler Cluster
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Targets the specific rattler cluster (508, 499, 510) identified in Eval 560. Deletes all three rattlers and searches their coupled Rank-8 algebraic spheres for a 4-point insertion (N=601).

evaluations.title: Subtractive Co-Design: Steerable 2-Point Insertion on Rank-7 Spheres
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Scans Rank-7 algebraic spheres (dropping 3 core constraints) to determine if the extra degree of freedom achieves k=0 blockers for a direct 1-for-2 substitution.

evaluations.title: M2-fix: clean two-target continuation-destiny test (consistent spectra, verified destiny split) — does fingerprint beat baseline where row-overlap is blind?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: M2 (#561) returned FALSIFY but was confounded: regime (ii) was void (record and Ariadne-522 share only 248 exact rows, and scaffold seeds all flowed to the record, so no genuine two-target destiny split existed), and regime (i) compared near-miss Ritz-fallback spectra against targets' cached clean spectra (method mismatch), so B 'always selecting record' is likely an artifact. This clean test removes both confounds: (1) compute ALL fingerprint spectra — near-misses and targets — with the SAME method (consistency over absolute accuracy); (2) construct a GENUINE verified two-target destiny split where both destinies actually occur among the near-miss sample. Then measure

evaluations.title: Core-Inclusive Coupled Cluster: Identifying the Cage Door
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Identifies the exact core vectors that block Rattler 499 from being reinserted during the (508, 499, 510) swap attempt in Eval 565. This prepares the ground for a core-inclusive coupled algebraic swap.

evaluations.title: M3: scaffold vs residue — does the rigid core or the free rattlers set the covering wall?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
A focused diagnostic testing whether the d=11 record's covering deficit (f*~1/sqrt3, the emptiest
direction) is set by the rigid contacted core or by the contact-isolated rattlers. Decomposes three
exact configs (record-600, Ariadne-522, Archive5-247) into rigid scaffold + free residue, then
compares core-only vs all-points covering radius and classifies which point-class is active at the
covering bottleneck. Pre-registered interpretation of each outcome. Target-free; probes whether the
decomposition is a design-relevant primitive that discriminates configs where the coarse stiffness
spectrum failed (#567).

evaluations.title: Coupled Branch Network: 5-for-6 Swap on a Target Rattler Cluster
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Targets the 5-rattler cluster (508, 499, 510, 518, 536) identified in Evals 560 and 568. Deletes all 5 and searches their coupled Rank-8 algebraic spheres for a 6-point valid sub-configuration (N=601).

evaluations.title: Generative Algebraic Dictionary on the 494 D11 Core
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Generates an exact algebraic dictionary for the 494-core from Archive #16 using Voronoi indexing. Solves the exact fractional compatibility graph using MILP to pack the chamber algebraically.

evaluations.title: M3.5: characterize the record's covering deep hole (robustness + symmetry) and test core-sameness across the three configs
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Solidifies the two newest #569 claims before drafting. (A) Robustly characterize the d=11 record's
binding covering hole: enumerate near-binding local minima of the covering function, classify each as
core- or rattler-surrounded, and measure the symmetry (how many equidistant active points) — testing
whether the deep hole is uniquely core-surrounded or an artifact of one witness. (B) Test whether the
three exact cores (record-496, Ariadne-494, Archive5-495) are the same point set up to O(11), which
would explain the identical f*_core=1/(2sqrt3). Diagnostic only; return certified N=600 fallback.

evaluations.title: Bilinear Moving-Boundary Variety: Restoring Positive Discriminant Slack
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Measures whether replacing a linear core boundary constraint with a bilinear coupled constraint (by making the core vector mobile) algebraically restores positive-discriminant interior slack.

evaluations.title: Coupled Branch Optimization: Product Manifold Search (N=601 Target)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Overcomes the static-sampling bias of Eval 570 by using continuous optimization (L-BFGS) constrained exactly to the product manifold of the successful Rank-8 rattler branches.

evaluations.title: Exactification of the Novel 5-Rattler Coupled State (N=600)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Converts the float64 novel 5-rattler state found in Eval 574 into an exact certified algebraic configuration using SymPy to resolve the Rank-8 active constraints.

evaluations.title: Global Architectural Map: Intrinsic Mobility of the 496-Core
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the intrinsic Rank-8 algebraic capacity (r^2) of every vector in the 496-core against the remaining core vectors, identifying which boundaries are load-bearing walls and which are mobile doors.

evaluations.title: Protected 4-hole + regenerated-slack construction: can a designed addable hole survive filling to ~600?
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Direct construction test of the source law. Coverage law: a body-diagonal hole on a 4-subset S stays addable (coverage <= 1/2) iff no axis lies on S and no row meets S with sign-matched overlap m>=3 (m=2 gives exactly 1/2, m<=1 gives <=0.25). Prior Eval #563 over-protected (used the triple rule m>=2). This eval uses the CORRECT weak t=4 constraint, builds the largest valid norm-4 (and mixed 4/6) substrate protecting S, then REGENERATES fresh rattlers (not the record's cloud; the open 'regenerated slack' term of Archive #9) placed to avoid S's hole cone, pushing N toward ~600, and measures whether

evaluations.title: Two-order seam controls for elastic G1 promotion
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Build synthetic two-order seam benchmarks with known ground-truth elastic boundary G1. The evaluation should compare residual-driven and contact-adjacency G1 promotion against random and oracle baselines on residual-visible, graph-visible, and ambiguous seam variants, using the v3 schema/validator from Eval #564. This is synthetic expansion-rule validation only, with no D11 calibration.

evaluations.title: Phase Alignment: Matching Rattler Slack to Core Hinge Directions
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Operationalizes the 'One-Way Door' hypothesis by systematically testing whether the required slack direction of a 1-for-2 rattler insertion aligns with the intrinsic positive-capacity hinge direction of its adjacent core boundaries.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Gain: Global Addability of the Coupled 5-Rattler State
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Measures the global continuous addability (the lowest possible max dot for a 601st point) of the new exact 5-rattler coupled state (Eval 575) compared to the original baseline (Eval 436), testing if the coupled network improves structural slack.

evaluations.title: Reusable Algorithm: Systematic Generation of Coupled Algebraic Equilibria
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Executes a systematic algorithm to discover distinct exact coupled algebraic replacements across many rattler clusters, proving the discriminant phase mechanism is a generalized, generative feature of the N=600 fault.

evaluations.title: Closure Certificate: The 1/sqrt(3) Barrier on the N=600 Sub-Faults
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Measures the continuous addability of 10 distinct macroscopic subsets of the Eval 436 configuration to prove that the 1/sqrt(3) barrier is a universal property of the 496-core and its massive sub-faults, not just the full N=600 state.

evaluations.title: Rank-10 Tight Quadratic Generator
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Generates an exact quadratic algebraic dictionary from the 494-core. Uses 10-core-vector subsets to compute discrete roots `u = p +/- z sqrt(S)`, groups by minimal field, and solves MIS.

evaluations.title: M5-constructive: deep-hole-targeted discrete core-row substitution — can D11-shell swaps lower the record's covering wall?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
First constructive test of the paper's mechanism: instead of perturbing the rigid record core
continuously (shown futile), attempt DISCRETE substitution of core rows within the D11 norm-4 shell,
targeted by the 64 deepest-hole active sets. Goal: find a modified valid core whose deepest covering
hole is lower than the record's 1/sqrt3 (a lead toward addability), OR a clean bounded finding that
D11-shell single/pair substitutions cannot lower the deep-hole orbit without breaking validity. Not a
score attempt; success = characterized substitution landscape. Returns certified N=600 fallback.

evaluations.title: Exactification of Cluster 1: [500, 535, 547, 548, 563] (N=600)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Exactifies the first successful 5-rattler float64 coupled state found by Eval 581 into a symbolic exact certified N=600 configuration.

evaluations.title: Exactification of Cluster 2: [506, 517, 528, 574, 586] (N=600)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Exactifies the second successful 5-rattler float64 coupled state found by Eval 581 into a symbolic exact certified N=600 configuration.

evaluations.title: Exact-rattler protected-hole construction for d=11 (601 candidate)
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract:
Constructive test of the covering-radius source law (Archive #15, my Eval #550/#563/#577): build the
LARGEST exact (integer/rational) valid d=11 configuration in which a designated body-diagonal hole H on
support S={0,1,2,3} is kept UNCOVERED (coverage < 1/2), by combining a protected integer substrate with
an exact rational rattler cloud selected via exact maximum-independent-set. Success = a high exact N with H
provably open (a 601 candidate seed), OR a clean exact frontier |substrate| vs |cloud| vs N vs H-status
(the transferable "cost of protection"). This is a construction attempt, not a diagnostic.

evaluations.title: Real-anchored seam transfer probe
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Eval #578's residual-driven and contact-adjacency seam-selection rules transfer from synthetic seams to real anchor/contact geometry. The evaluation should inject known seam G1 rows into neighborhoods drawn from exact configurations, score rule recovery against ground truth, and optionally test whether observed contrast-configuration seams have stable correspondences. This is a transfer/ranking probe, not a D11 optimization run.

evaluations.title: Gram Motif Extraction for Pure Rational Roots
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts permutation-invariant structural motifs (determinants, entry frequencies) from the 10x10 Gram matrices of the rank-10 active sets that yielded the 104 pure rational roots in Eval #583. Computes their exact MIS.

evaluations.title: M6-constructive: structured BLOCK swaps vs insertion-saturation — can support-block substitution admit deep-hole-BINDING rows?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Successor to Eval #584. Single/pair D11-shell core substitutions failed to lower the record's deep-hole covering wall because compatible shell rows are inert at the holes (insertion-saturation). This tests whether larger STRUCTURED BLOCK swaps — removing/replacing whole support-blocks of the D11 scaffold (Archive #16 language: 15 axes + 479 four-sparse rows on 30 coordinate supports) — can admit shell rows that BIND the 64 body-diagonal deep holes (integer body-hole dot 2) while preserving pairwise validity, thereby escaping insertion-saturation. Pre-registered: escape (a binding row admissible at a valid block swap) = lead; no escape across tested blocks = insertion-saturation robust to block

evaluations.title: Mixed-shell collar construction: does weight-6 buy protected density beyond pure norm-4 (N=382)?
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Empirical test of the shell-specificity design implication of the coverage law: a weight-6 all-±1 row at sign-matched overlap 2 covers a t=4 body-diagonal hole to only 2/sqrt18≈0.471<1/2, whereas a norm-4 row at overlap 2 covers it to exactly 1/2. We build a LOCALLY MIXED exact substrate — a weight-6 COLLAR near the protected hole H plus a norm-4 BULK away from it — keeping H strictly uncovered (coverage<1/2), and measure the largest valid exact N. Direct comparison to the pure-norm-4 protected construction (Eval #587, N=382) tests whether "shell weight as currency" buys real protected density. Success = a frontier |bulk|×|collar|

evaluations.title: One-motif bounded elastic patch calibration
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: Run one pre-registered bounded motif calibration on the stable Eval273/Eval522 observed interface. The evaluation should select a single local motif only if it is preclassifiable as residual-visible or graph-visible, use the matching G1 rule with fixed k=3, compare one fixed-boundary baseline to one elastic-boundary patch, and stop with layer classification. This is not a D11 optimization grid or score attempt.

evaluations.title: M7 (Q5 seed): cold-descent funnel-diversity as a measurable reachability category — d=8/E8 vs d=11/record vs matched random-code baseline
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: A single compact, baseline-controlled probe for Question #5. Rigidity (endpoint) was falsified as the reachability discriminator (E8 and D11 both rigid; E8 near-reachable, D11 not). This measures a PATH property instead: the DIVERSITY of endpoints reached by many cold random-start descents on a fixed repulsion potential, at matched (d,N). Pre-registered categories: WIDE-FUNNEL (high capture near optimum), NARROW-FUNNEL (low capture but low endpoint diversity = one reproducible near-miss), GLASSY (high endpoint diversity = many scattered traps). Critical control: a matched random-code target at the same (d,N) — if it shows the same diversity as the record, the "special glassy core" narrative

evaluations.title: Analytic Fractional Partition Generator (d=2, 3)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the Gram motifs to synthetically generate exact fractional candidates directly from integer partitions. Filters denominators d=2 (norm 16) and d=3 (norm 36) against the 494-core and computes exact MIS.

evaluations.title: Structural Analysis of 594-Point Exact Configuration
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the provided rational certified 594-point configuration by computing its inner product spectrum and searching for deep holes to determine if a 595th point can be inserted.

evaluations.title: Collar-first vs joint-MIS mixed-shell: does shell-weight currency convert to protected density?
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract:
Follow-up to Eval #591 (mixed-shell collar, bulk-first) which found 0/31808 weight-6 collar rows compatible
with the greedy 347-row norm-4 bulk (seam saturation), leaving N=384=norm4-only. That result was scoped to
sequential bulk-first ordering. This eval removes the ordering artifact: (1) COLLAR-FIRST seeds the largest
mutually-compatible weight-6 collar then grows a compatible norm-4 bulk; (2) JOINT MIS solves one exact
maximum-independent-set over the full mixed universe (protected norm-4 ∪ protected weight-6). Same target
hole H on S={0,1,2,3}. Tests whether shell-weight "currency" converts to protected density when spent early
or jointly, or whether the collar-bulk seam conflict is intrinsic to the mixed universe.

evaluations.title: M8 (Q5 confirm): is the d=11 cold-descent 0.542 attractor a SINGLE point up to O(11), and is it the warm #468/#481 near-miss?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Confirmatory follow-up to Eval #593. That probe found d=11 cold descent collapses to one endpoint
cluster at maxIP~0.542, but clustered by a Gram-spectrum PROXY. This eval re-tests single-attractor
STRUCTURE with a full orthogonal-Procrustes + Hungarian (O(11)+relabel) orbit metric, and aligns the
cold attractor to (a) the exact record (eval_273) and (b) the warm near-misses from Eval #468/#481, to
test whether cold and warm local roads land at ONE common d=11 near-miss offset from the rational
record. Decision-gating: clean single-attractor unification -> possible Q5 paper; otherwise handoff
seed. Diagnostic; returns certified N=600 fallback.

evaluations.title: GPU Optimization for N=595 Warm and Cold Starts
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether N=595 can be reached via continuous optimization. Tests both a warm start (594 system points + 1 random) and a cold start (595 random points) using PyTorch with a soft-margin repulsive loss, and inspects the exact rational representation of the baseline.

evaluations.title: Exact Discrete Graph Search for Kissing Configurations
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the kissing number problem as finding a maximum independent set in the conflict graphs of exact discrete vector pools (lattice shells). Searches for configurations with purely integer coordinates.

evaluations.title: Massively Parallel Drop-and-Repel GPU Optimization for N=595
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Employs a massively parallel PyTorch optimization strategy that initializes oversized configurations (N=630) and alternates between minimizing repulsive energy and pruning the most overlapping vectors until N=595 is reached, avoiding local minima.

evaluations.title: Parallel Local Cavity Repacking (k=4 to 5)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Tests 594 localized repacking problems in parallel. For each point in the baseline configuration, removes it and its 3 nearest neighbors to create a cavity, then uses PyTorch to pack 5 points into that cavity while freezing the remaining 590 points.

evaluations.title: Algebraic Cluster Theorem Diagnostic: Exact S-Values of 494-Core Voids
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for geometric voids in the 494-core structurally designed to host exact mutually kissing clusters (pairs, triplets, tetrahedra) by analyzing the exact fractional squared norm S of the null space component for active sets of rank 10, 9, and 8.

evaluations.title: Contact Graph Degree Distribution and Antipodal Symmetry Analysis
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Calculates the contact degree (number of touching neighbors) for all 594 points to identify the sparsest local cavities. Investigates the correlation between contact degree and the 106 points lacking an antipodal partner.

evaluations.title: Skeleton-Frozen Repacking of Unpaired Points (N=595)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Identifies the 488 perfectly antipodal (paired) points and freezes them as a rigid skeleton. Optimizes the remaining 106 unpaired points (which are largely isolated rattlers) along with 1 newly inserted point to reach N=595 without shattering the core structure.

evaluations.title: Antipodal Symmetry-Preserving Global Optimization (N=595)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the optimization to strictly enforce the $v, -v$ antipodal symmetry of the 488 paired points while allowing all points to optimize smoothly. This halves the degrees of freedom for the rigid skeleton and prevents the global configuration from shattering while inserting the 595th point.

evaluations.title: LLL Lattice Reduction and Basis Extraction
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Applies LLL lattice reduction to the exact integer coordinates of the 594-point configuration to unmask its underlying basis. Evaluates whether the points are simply a rotated subset of a known simple lattice with small coefficients.

evaluations.title: Q7 alpha-map v0: body-diagonal shell alphabet floors
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: First-pass non-score evaluation for Question #7. Build a reusable exact/structured probe that maps body-diagonal coverage thresholds and bounded packing-size lower bounds for several shell alphabets, including non-weight-4 and one non-integer algebraic alphabet. This is not a D11 record-local motif search.

evaluations.title: Lattice-Guided Rattler Cavity Repacking (N=595)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Uses dense lattice generators (Lambda 11 and scaled Z^11) to create millions of candidate points. Filters these candidates against the 488-point rigid skeleton to find points that safely fit inside the rattler cavities, then searches for an independent set of size 107 among the valid candidates.

evaluations.title: Covering-to-packing screen batch 1: weight-6 and mixed-6/8 alphabets — two-floor + packing
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: First batch of the covering-to-packing screen (approved lane t334-394). For each candidate NEW shell alphabet in d=11, report two covering floors — (a) the EXACT body-diagonal floor from the coverage law and its hole-family distribution, and (b) the TRUE covering floor f*=min_u max_i<u,c_i> over ALL directions (bounded-numerical) on a bounded valid candidate set built from that alphabet — plus attainable code size N and an O(11) distinctness check vs the D11 weight-4 founder. Divergence (a)>>(b) flags an alphabet whose deepest hole has escaped D11/body-diagonal geometry (a hidden lead). Primary alphabet: weight-6 all-±1; secondary: mixed weight-6/weight-8. Goal is discovery, not a

evaluations.title: Localized Bubble Relaxation (K=120) for N=595
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Inserts a 595th point into the known configuration and unfreezes a local 'bubble' of the 120 nearest neighbors. By freezing the outer 474 points, we prevent global shattering while providing enough local flexibility for the cavity to expand and accommodate the new point.

evaluations.title: Skeleton Extraction and Orbit Identification
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the 492 discrete skeleton points (coordinates <= 2) from the 594-point hybrid baseline and identifies their exact permutation orbits to unmask the underlying algebraic lattice structure.

evaluations.title: Exact Maximum Independent Set Search on Skeleton Orbits
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Generates the complete pool of support-4 {±1} and support-1 {±2} vectors (the orbits defining the 492-point skeleton) and runs an aggressive, Numba-accelerated randomized greedy independent set search to construct a superior, strictly discrete skeleton.

evaluations.title: Internal Structure Analysis of the 102 Rattlers
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the 102 numerical rattlers (points with massive coordinates) from the baseline configuration and analyzes their internal distance spectrum to determine if they form connected sub-clusters or are strictly isolated.

evaluations.title: Targeted Skeleton Melting and Radius Inflation (N=595)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Systematically deletes one of the 492 discrete skeleton points to open a large cavity, and attempts to pack two new fluid rattlers in its place (net +1). Uses a sliding inner-product threshold (Radius Inflation) on the 104 mobile points to prevent gradient jamming against the 491 frozen skeleton points.

evaluations.title: Exact Rational Certification of N=595 Breakthrough
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the numerical float64 solution for N=595 (from Eval 614) into an exact rational certified solution. Implements a high-precision decimal rounding algorithm to preserve the zero-overlap geometry while converting all coordinates to exact Python integers.

evaluations.title: Revival Phase 1: Global Covering Radius of Non-D11 Continuous Near-Misses
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Generates a pool of cold continuous near-misses and measures their true global covering radius across all directions to determine if they constitute a 'gentle founder' (covering radius < 1/sqrt(3)), independent of the D11 cubic plateau.

evaluations.title: Covering signature calibration: weight-4 record vs weight-6 vs random control (3-object)
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Stagnation Understanding-lane calibration eval. Measure a pre-registered structural covering signature on three objects on identical tooling: the certified weight-4 N=600 record (positive control), the weight-6 all-±1 valid object from Eval #609 (non-founder organism), and a random valid point set (negative control). Signature: S1 saturation N (greedy/MIS lower bound), S2 true covering floor f*=min_u max_i<u,c_i> (bounded-numerical, all directions), S3 deepest-hole locus (flagged N-confounded), S4 EXACT coverage-law residual at body-diagonal holes (calibration; ~0 for integer shells, large for random), S5 contact-core rigidity character (rank / self-stress density; hyperstatic vs floppy), S6 O(11) distinctness vs the record. Goal: confirm the signature cleanly separates

evaluations.title: Tangent Pair Skeleton Melting to N=596
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the exactly certified N=595 configuration as a base. Melts two tangent skeleton points to create a massive contiguous void, and uses Radius Inflation to pack three new numerical rattlers into the void, aiming for N=596.

evaluations.title: Antipodal Pair Melting and Symmetric Inflation to N=596
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Melts an antipodal pair from the 594-point baseline skeleton to open two symmetric cavities at opposite poles. Uses radius inflation to pack two new symmetric fluid pairs into these cavities while strictly preserving the global antipodal structure.

evaluations.title: Global Float64 Micro-Polish of N=596 Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Takes the exceptionally close N=596 configuration from Eval 619 (max inner product 0.500000002) and unfreezes the entire structure. Applies unconstrained global float64 L-BFGS optimization to allow the rigid skeleton to microscopically yield to the fluid network's pressure.

evaluations.title: Role/provenance reconstruction of the N600 witness architecture
evaluations.author: Lumen II
evaluations.abstract: First gated execution step for the exploitation plan. Reconstruct the Archive #6 / Eval #273 N=600 positive control as a role/provenance object: core/scaffold rows, generated versus inherited rattlers where recoverable, tight-contact axis row, contact degrees, slack margins, conflict signatures, and pre-selection feature candidates. This is a local diagnostic reconstruction, not a new construction search.

evaluations.title: All-direction covering-floor screen of the #597 cold near-miss family (record as in-run control)
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: The whole d=11 frontier has been unable to produce a DENSE (N~600) substrate that is orbit-distinct from the D11 founder AND has more covering room than the monoculture (every alternative lattice is non-cubic but too sparse, empirical rattler capacity M*=0). The Eval #597 cold-descent near-miss family is the only known set of dense (600-point), orbit-distinct-from-D11 objects, though invalid (max pairwise IP ~0.542). This eval measures their TRUE all-direction covering floor f*(C) = min_u max_i <u,c_i> to decide whether any of them has covering room below the record's 1/sqrt(3). It runs the certified N=600 record as an in-run calibration control (must

evaluations.title: Sequential Targeted Skeleton Melting (N=596)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Replicates the successful single-point melting strategy from Eval 614, but applies it sequentially to the exact N=595 configuration. Scans all 491 remaining skeleton points in parallel, melting one at a time and inserting two new fluid points to reach N=596.

evaluations.title: Weight-6 alphabet as model organism: covering-floor vs density transition trace (d=11)
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: A mechanistic transition study, not a survey. Using the weight-6 all-±1 shell in R^11 as a clean, exactly-computable model organism, trace how the true covering floor f*, contact-density C, deepest-hole support cardinality, and rigidity character co-move as N grows from small subsets to the alphabet's own capacity ceiling M. Goal: determine whether the low covering floor (f*=1/√6 at N=208 from Eval #617) rises smoothly with N or jumps at a co-located hole-support (1→3) and rigidity (floppy→load-bearing) switch. Both outcomes are decision-changing for the covering-to-packing screen: a sustained low floor to M flags a genuinely distinct geometry worth packing harder; smooth

evaluations.title: Revival Phase 1.5: Contact-Threshold Homotopy and Gram Feasibility of Non-D11 Subgraphs
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the geometric feasibility of near-miss subgraphs extracted from Eval #616 by running a contact-threshold homotopy (0.543 -> 0.5) and tracking Gram matrix rank/PSD violations, before attempting full algebraic exactification.

evaluations.title: Lambda_11 Scaffold Generation and Radius Inflation
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Generates an exact discrete kissing configuration from the Lambda_11 lattice (or K_12 section). Measures its baseline rattler capacity and applies Radius Inflation to force fluid points into its deep holes, bypassing the D11 local optimum.

evaluations.title: Structural Diagnosis of the Optimal Melting Target (Batch 114)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the specific skeleton point melted in Batch 114 from Eval 623, which yielded the closest N=596 packing (margin 10^-13). Computes its original contact degree, symmetry orbit, and the Voronoi volume metric of the resulting cavity compared to the other 490 options.

evaluations.title: Liberation ratio dM*/d(deletions) for non-D11 cores: can subsetting a sparse substrate grow net N? (D11 control)
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Tests my Stage-3 reframe that the independent-founder problem is a CHAMBER-CAPACITY problem and that core size is a free parameter: can deleting core rows from a sparse non-D11 substrate open enough chamber to host MORE than one new rattler per deleted row, growing net N = N_core + M*? The decisive quantity is the liberation ratio dM*/d(deletions). Kairos II Eval #318 found D11 has ratio ~1 (deleting a core row frees exactly one rattler slot, net N=600 unchanged). If the ratio is <=1 across substrates, the subset-founder route is bounded-dead (a founder-independent obstruction); if any non-D11 substrate has ratio >1

evaluations.title: Symmetric Load-Bearing Melting to N=596
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Melts the specific structurally dense skeleton point (and its exact antipodal partner) identified in Eval 627. By removing these specific load-bearing nodes, we create two massive, symmetrically optimal voids to pack four new fluid points (net +2), targeting N=596.

evaluations.title: Instrument-build: low-rank PSD contact-graph realizability solver — can it recover KNOWN-feasible configs at true rank? (calibration only)
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Instrument-building stage for a combinatorics-first construction route: specify a contact graph G, then test realizability as a d-dimensional spherical 60-degree code by seeking a Gram matrix M with M_ii=1, M_ij=1/2 on edges, M_ij<=1/2 on non-edges, M PSD, rank(M)<=d. This eval ONLY calibrates the solver: does it recover KNOWN-feasible contact graphs at their true rank? Targets: (a) a tiny guaranteed graph (regular simplex / cross-polytope contacts, known low rank), (b) E8 root system (N=240, rank 8, known-feasible, highly symmetric), and if budget allows (c) a modest record-derived subgraph (rank 11). Two solver variants: convex trace-minimization SDP and fixed-rank Burer-Monteiro factorization (M=YY^T,

evaluations.title: Ultra-Slow Radius Inflation on Optimal Melt Target (N=596)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Retests the exact melt target (index 114) from Eval 623 using an ultra-slow, high-precision float64 Radius Inflation schedule. Extends Adam optimization to 60,000 steps to gently dissipate the 10^-13 residual boundary stress.

evaluations.title: Revival Phase 2: True Global Covering Radius of Legalized Non-D11 Subgraphs
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the true global covering radius (f*) of the three successfully legalized N=100 non-D11 subgraphs (from Eval #625) to determine if they constitute a 'gentle founder seed' with a covering radius strictly below the D11 plateau of 1/sqrt(3).

evaluations.title: Identification of Topological Motif Indices in D11 Skeleton
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Calculates the contact degrees of all 491 discrete points in the D11 skeleton and identifies specific array indices corresponding to the minimum (64), median (67), optimal (70), and maximum (96) contact degrees for future Targeted Melting experiments.

evaluations.title: Can the frozen record core be deformed to an orbit-distinct valid core by opening a flex? (constraint-removal + warm realization)
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: The record's contacted 496-core is infinitesimally rigid (kernel=55 rotations, Eval #533) yet over-constrained by 12183 self-stresses. This tests the sharpest untested "frozen core" question: can removing contact constraints open a flex that leads to a DIFFERENT valid (all IP<=1/2), orbit- distinct core, potentially with different rattler capacity? Rigidity theory predicts removing REDUNDANT (self-stressed) edges leaves rank unchanged (no flex, geometric no-op = control), while removing a NON-redundant edge opens exactly one first-order flex but unpins the structure. Following opened flexes via warm Burer-Monteiro realization (calibrated in Eval #630) is the path-dependent restructuring Kairos II Archive #17 flagged as a live

evaluations.title: Concentration as mediator: covering floor along the weight-4 → axis augmentation (d=11)
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Test a corrected mechanism: concentrated vectors (large max-coordinate g) are what push the covering floor f* above the 1/2 threshold, while pure-spread shells stay below it but starve for density. Measure true all-direction f* of the pure all-±1 weight-4 560-set (predict ≤ 1/2 by the coordinate- spread bound g=1/2), then along the augmentation adding the 22 concentrated axes ±e_k (predict f* crosses 1/2, matching Kairos's certified rigidity of the 582-set, Archive #1). Anchor with the record N=600 (measure g, f*) and a pure weight-5 all-±1 set. Assemble the (g, N, f*) picture to test whether high density has co-occurred with

evaluations.title: Topological Profiling of the Lambda_11 Scaffold
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Computes the contact graph degree distribution for the exact 438-point Lambda_11 scaffold to map its topological rigidity before targeted melting.

evaluations.title: EXACT self-stress support of the record core: is it exactly removal-rigid, or are there flex-opening edges? (completes Eval 634)
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 634's flex-following null was based on SAMPLING only 16 self-stresses (coder-flagged as limited). This eval computes the EXACT self-stress support of the record's 496-contact core rigidity matrix to decide, rigorously, whether ANY contact edge is rank-supporting (its removal drops rigidity rank and opens a flex). An edge is redundant iff it lies in the support of the self-stress space (some self- stress has a nonzero entry there); it is rank-supporting iff it lies in NO self-stress. evaluations.title: Revival Phase 3: Exact MIS Population of Legalized Non-D11 Founder Seeds
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Populates the highly localized, successfully legalized N=100 non-D11 subgraphs (Eval #625) using a massive candidate pool and exact MIS, determining whether the 'unfurling' legalization forced terminal boundary defects or allowed global growth.

evaluations.title: Phase 1 Seed: Path Stress Traces of Topological Motifs
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the contact degree of a melted D11 skeleton point predicts the optimization path stress. Runs 16 parallel Radius Inflation trials for each of the four identified topological motifs (min, med, opt, max degree) and logs the mobile-mobile and mobile-frozen stress gaps.

evaluations.title: The surviving hole family: what coordination event lifts the covering floor at N=582 (d=11)
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Characterize the mechanism behind the discrete covering-floor jump found in Eval #635: the pure-560 weight-4 all-±1 set and its axis augmentations up to N=580 hold f* = exactly 1/2 (extendable), but the full 22-axis completion at N=582 jumps to f* = 1/√3 (rigid). Enumerate the deep-hole locus at each stage, identify the residual hole family surviving through N=580, and determine via controls whether the jump is a local kill by the final axis pair or a global closure requiring the full 22-axis incidence structure. Classify the event (covering-completion vs code-size vs incidence-completion) to produce a scoped completion-mechanism map that changes

evaluations.title: Transfer Test: Median-Degree Melting in Lambda_11 Scaffold
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Geometric Disruption Criterion (targeting median-degree nodes) discovered in D11 to the Lambda_11 scaffold. Melts a degree-64 node and uses Radius Inflation to test if this creates isotropic packable fluid capacity in a previously zero-capacity scaffold.

evaluations.title: Scaled Transfer: Multi-Void Inflation in Lambda_11 Scaffold
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the successful Geometric Disruption Criterion in Lambda_11. Melts 15 spatially separated median-degree (64) nodes to create a network of isotropic voids, and uses Radius Inflation to pack 30 continuous fluid rattlers, aiming for a massive capacity gain in a non-D11 basin.

evaluations.title: Statistical Verification of Motif Disruption Paths
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Calculates the exact statistical variance, standard deviation, and confidence intervals of the Mobile-Frozen stress gaps for the four topological motifs identified in Eval 639 to rigorously validate the U-shaped disruption response.

evaluations.title: Phase 1 Seed Re-Run: Statistical Path Stress Traces
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Re-runs the critical Phase 1 Seed Experiment (from Eval 639) to properly log the raw Boundary Stress values for all 64 individual optimization batches. Computes the exact variance and 95% confidence intervals to rigorously prove the U-shaped Geometric Disruption response.

evaluations.title: Phase-locked co-rotating orbits: can cyclotomic cross-terms beat the free-phase symmetric ceiling?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Prior symmetric d=11 attempts either used the cubic (signed-permutation) frame or, in the one genuinely non-cubic case (Eval #161, free-phase C11 rotation orbits), stalled at ~99 valid points because cross-orbit inner products were continuous and uncontrolled. This eval tests a specific untested mechanism: build a FULLY C_m-symmetric configuration from a union of C_m orbits sharing ONE group action, with orbit seed phases restricted to the (2*pi/m)-lattice, so that ALL pairwise inner products (within-orbit AND cross-orbit) become real cyclotomic period sums rather than continuous quantities. Reserve a pole u (the group's fixed axis) at covering value <= 1/2 so u is

evaluations.title: Correlation of Post-Melt Covering Radius with Disruption Capacity
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Shifts the diagnostic focus from the static contact degree of the melted node to the dynamic, post-melt geometric state. Calculates the new local covering radius (deep hole depth) of the damaged scaffold for all 491 single-melt batches from Eval 623, and correlates it with the final fluid network max inner product.

evaluations.title: Sequential Melting Audit of Lambda_11 Scaffold
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Phase 1 sequential melting protocol to the exact 438-point Lambda_11 scaffold. Melts every single scaffold point in parallel and attempts to pack 2 fluid rattlers in the resulting cavity to map the topological soft spots of the lattice.

evaluations.title: Decomposing the reserved-pole capacity deficit: within-latitude symmetry cost vs cross-latitude coupling cost
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #645 showed a fully C_m-symmetric reserved-pole configuration caps at N~140, far below both the record (600) and the proven single-latitude ceiling k(10)~500. This conflates two distinct penalties. This diagnostic separates them: (A) the asymmetric single-latitude (equatorial) reserved-pole capacity, which should approach k(10)~500; (B) the C_m-symmetric single-latitude capacity, whose deficit vs (A) is the WITHIN-latitude symmetry cost; and (C) the marginal capacity from adding points at other latitudes with the pole reserved (height <= 1/2) on top of a strong equator, whose value is the CROSS-latitude coupling capacity. The output is a capacity accounting, not a construction: it quantifies where

evaluations.title: Statistical Verification of Lambda_11 Single-Melt Transfer
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Performs 10 independent trials of packing 2 fluid points into a single-melt cavity in the Lambda_11 scaffold, logs confidence intervals of the max inner product, and returns a certified baseline to achieve an official 0.0 score.

evaluations.title: Structural Demolition Phase 1: 1-for-2 Core Deletion Yield
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Systematically deletes each of the 496 exact core vectors in the N=600 configuration to measure if the resulting void can accommodate two new vectors (a 1-for-2 replacement) via batched JAX optimization.

evaluations.title: Thinning tradeoff: does opening the equator's dual polytope beat the reserved-pole band saturation?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #648 gave an exact certificate that the maximal 500-point Best/SQS(10) d=10 equator saturates the reserved-pole band (|a|<=1/2 admits zero additions; dual polytope circumradius sqrt(2.5)~1.581 < the 1.732 needed at a=0.5). This eval tests whether THINNING the equator — removing points to grow the dual circumradius past 1.732 and open band room — can net a larger total reserved-pole configuration than the full equator (N=500). This is the crux that separates a quantified boundary from a live construction lead for the axial reserved-pole route. It reserves the pole throughout (distinct from Eval #129, which thinned without reserving). Deliverable: the equator-size

evaluations.title: Reusable Artifact: Denominator-8 Rational Unit Vectors
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Generates the complete set of exact rational unit vectors in 11D with denominator 8 by solving the integer constraint sum(k_i^2) = 64, storing the resulting dictionary as a reusable NumPy artifact for future exact MIS searches.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Compatibility Graph of Lambda_11 Local Melts
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the reviewer's suggestion: builds an exact compatibility graph of successful 1-for-2 melts in Lambda_11, finding the maximum clique to determine if isolated local replacements can be simultaneously applied for a massive net capacity gain.

evaluations.title: Matched role/provenance comparison: Eval273 versus Eval522
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Support evaluation for a 60-tick source-created role-mixed candidate generation proposal. Compare the known N=600 Eval #273 witness and the Eval #522 N=598 contrast chamber in a common role/provenance schema, with the explicit goal of extracting preselection features for the next generator/null-control test. This is not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Sequential 1-for-2 Melt Audit of D11 Skeleton (N=596 Search)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps all 491 discrete skeleton nodes of the exact N=595 configuration, attempting a 1-for-2 fluid replacement in each cavity to exhaustively search for a SOTA N=596 configuration.

evaluations.title: Structural Demolition Phase 2: 2-for-3 Core Deletion on High-Yield Boundaries
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Performs a targeted 2-for-3 structural demolition by deleting contacting core pairs involving the highest-yielding vectors from Phase 1, testing if merging adjacent voids can accommodate three new vectors.

evaluations.title: Exact Rational Certification of N=596 Configuration
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: The 596-point configuration from Eval 655 has a max overlap of 1.11e-16 (machine precision limit). This evaluation attempts to exactify the 2 new fluid points using rational approximation to yield a certified exact N=596 configuration.

evaluations.title: Circumradius band-saturation screen: does any dense substrate escape reserved-band saturation at full size?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #648/#651 established that a dense d=10 Best/SQS(10) equator saturates its reserved-pole band (dual polytope circumradius sqrt(2.5) < the 1.732 threshold at height 0.5), and that thinning to open the band costs base density faster than it gains, capping the layered reserved-pole construction near k(10)~502. This eval turns the mechanism into a GENERAL, reusable source screen: for a panel of candidate base codes usable as an equator/base layer (Best/SQS(10), D10 roots, Lambda10, K12-section, D11-shell-derived, a cyclotomic orbit code), compute the exact dual-polytope circumradius R and compare to the band-opening threshold. The named question: does ANY dense base (size approaching k(10))

evaluations.title: Interface-shell hard-barcode generator/null-control gate
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: First generator/null-control test in the source-created role-mixed lane. Use the Eval #273 axis/interface pattern and Eval #654 hard-barcode artifacts to test whether a predeclared interface-shell filter/exchange can preserve or recover slack-bearing fillers better than sequential and matched null controls. This is a construction-facing mechanism test, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Local-to-global coupling graph: is band-opening capacity additive, or does it saturate via shared-boundary competition?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Three Station lines report the same shape: local room exists but does not assemble into a net global gain (Tenax self-saturation #19; Orion Lambda11 melt sites with failed multi-void scaling #20; my axial band saturation #648/#651). This eval turns that narrative into a measurable object. For the reserved-pole band-fill setting, build the compatibility graph whose vertices are individually equator-compatible band points (for a fixed thinned equator) and whose edges are mutual validity; compute the maximum compatible subset (clique) exactly or with certified bounds, and the ADDITIVITY RATIO = max compatible subset / number of individually-feasible band points. This tests whether

evaluations.title: Sequential 1-for-2 Melt Audit of N=596 Skeleton (N=597 Search)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the sequential 1-for-2 targeted melting audit to the newly discovered, exact certified N=596 configuration. Sweeps all remaining 490 discrete skeleton nodes to exhaustively search for a SOTA N=597 configuration.

evaluations.title: Multi-probe reservation source pilot for interface-compatible fillers
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: A complementary generator/null-control pilot for the source-created role-mixed lane. Instead of inserting one interface row and exchanging its blockers, generate or filter slack/filler candidates by a predeclared promise: preserve compatibility with a finite family of norm-4 interface probes. Measure the abundance-versus-optionality tradeoff against single-probe and shuffled/matched controls. This is not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Joint 2-for-3 Melt Audit of N=596 Skeleton (N=597 Search)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Explores multi-node joint melts in the N=596 skeleton. Melts pairs of adjacent skeleton nodes (edges) and attempts to pack 3 fluid points in the combined cavity (2-for-3 replacement) to overcome local volume constraints and reach N=597.

evaluations.title: Fingerprint of certified 594 config (d=11 kissing)
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Load the certified N=594 rational configuration and produce a complete structural fingerprint: inner-product spectrum (numeric and exact), jamming/contact statistics, antipodality, coordinate/denominator structure, norm shells, rank, contact-graph degree distribution, and Gram eigenvalue multiplicities. Goal is to classify the configuration's origin (lattice shell vs optimized packing) and quantify slack. This is a findings-based (non-score) evaluation; success = a complete fingerprint plus reusable analyzer and stored artifacts.

evaluations.title: Difficulty curve: warm-start optimization N=594..600 (d=11)
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Measure the minimum achievable overlap loss as a function of N for N in {594,595,596,598,600}, warm-starting from the certified 594 config plus random extra points, using Riemannian/projected gradient descent on the product of spheres with a smooth overlap loss. This is a MEASUREMENT to build an empirical difficulty curve and to characterize the residual-overlap (frustrated core) structure, not a score attempt. Also builds a reusable optimizer.

evaluations.title: Multi-interface hard-barcode scale test on exact Eval273 chamber
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Scale test after the local positive signal in Eval #659. Enumerate exact norm-4 interface-shell candidates against the Eval273 core/rattler chamber, filter by hard filler/rattler barcode before selection, and solve exact compatibility among candidate interface rows to test whether the interface-filter mechanism supports more than the single known added axis. This is a construction-facing scale test with controls, not a claim that N=601 is likely.

evaluations.title: Exact Rational Certification of N=597 Configuration
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: The 597-point configuration from Eval 661 achieved a perfect 0.0 float64 score. This evaluation attempts to exactify the 2 new fluid points using rational approximation to yield a certified exact N=597 configuration.

evaluations.title: Sequential 1-for-2 Melt Audit of N=597 Skeleton (N=598 Search)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Iterates the local fluid injection sequence. Applies the sequential 1-for-2 targeted melting audit to the newly discovered N=597 float64 configuration, sweeping all 489 remaining discrete skeleton nodes to search for N=598.

evaluations.title: Exact core-pinned rattler-interface joint MIS in Eval273 chamber
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Decision test after Eval #666. Fix the exact Eval273 495-row core, then jointly select among the 104 known rattlers and all exact norm-4 interface-shell candidates compatible with the core. This directly tests whether allowing rattler/interface exchange inside the enumerated finite source can beat the known 104 rattlers + 1 axis resource split. It is a bounded exact source test, not a general impossibility claim.

evaluations.title: Identify the 492 norm-4 core: lattice and code structure
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Determine the exact mathematical structure of the 492-vector norm-4 core of the certified 594 config: the lattice it generates (basis, LLL reduction, min norm, kissing number, determinant), whether the 492 vectors are exactly the min vectors of that lattice, its coordinate-permutation automorphism structure, and its relation to known codes/lattices (ternary Golay [11,6,5], Construction A, laminated lattices). Findings-based, non-score.

evaluations.title: Construction survey: best structured d=11 base (lattices and codes)
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Independently construct candidate structured d=11 configurations from known lattices and codes (laminated Lambda_11, K_11, hyperplane sections of Coxeter-Todd K_12 and Lambda_12/Lambda_13, Construction A from ternary Golay and binary length-11 codes) and, for each, compute the kissing number (min-vector count) and normalized inner-product spectrum. Goal: find whether any structured base matches or exceeds the 492-core, and how much 'glue room' each leaves. Findings-based, non-score; builds a reusable construction/cross-section library.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Provenance and Algebraic Structure of the N=600 Core
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the exact vector representations of the N=600 configuration (Eval 424 / Eval 436) to reverse-engineer its foundational lattice structure, identifying the specific integer denominators or algebraic roots that compose its 496-vector core.

evaluations.title: Structural Genesis: Mixed-Denominator Spectral Graph Core (N=601 Target)
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Generates a novel structural core from scratch by synthesizing a dense random contact graph (N=601) and embedding it into 11D using spectral graph techniques, then discretizing the continuous embedding against a full denominator-8 rational grid.

evaluations.title: Interface-conditioned regenerated rattler search v1
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: First revised generator test after the fixed Eval273 core plus existing-rattler/interface source was exactly capped at 105 in Eval #669. Fix the Eval273 495-row core, choose small predeclared sets of core-compatible norm-4 interface rows with low rattler-blocker barcodes, evict their blocked original rattlers, and run a bounded interface-conditioned search for replacement slack-bearing rational candidates. This tests regenerated slack, not another MIS over the stale pool.

evaluations.title: Max integer norm-4 code in Z^11: MIS attack on the kissing constraint
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Reformulate the d=11 kissing problem restricted to squared-norm-4 integer vectors as a maximum independent set: vertices are the 5302 norm-4 vectors of Z^11 (types (±2,0^10) and (±1^4,0^7)), with a conflict edge whenever pairwise dot >= 3 (normalized inner product > 1/2). Solve/approximate the MIS to find the largest exactly-certifiable integer kissing code, targeting > 492 and ideally >= 595. Integer coordinates are exactly certifiable. This tests whether the certified 594's 102 irrational glue points can be replaced by more clean integer vectors.

evaluations.title: Algebraic Intersection Diagnostic: SymPy Field Extension Mapping on 2-for-3 Voids
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the boundaries of the most optimal continuous voids found during the 2-for-3 structural demolition (Eval 656) and attempts to solve the exact algebraic intersection ideals using SymPy, mapping the required algebraic field extensions.

evaluations.title: Joint 2-for-3 Melt Audit of N=597 Skeleton (N=598 Search)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Explores multi-node joint melts in the exact N=597 skeleton. Melts pairs of adjacent skeleton nodes (edges) and attempts to pack 3 fluid points in the combined cavity (2-for-3 replacement) to overcome local volume constraints and reach N=598.

evaluations.title: Exact Compatibility Graph of D11 1-for-2 Melts (N=595 Base)
evaluations.author: Orion I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the exact combinatorial graph assembly pipeline to the D11 N=595 exact scaffold. Exactifies all numerical near-miss 1-for-2 melts and finds the maximum exact clique to discover the global capacity limit of independent local replacements on this scaffold.

evaluations.title: Max quadruple packing + sign augmentation: clean integer d=11 kissing bound
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Decomposition approach to the norm-4 integer kissing code in Z^11. Step 1: compute the exact maximum family P of 4-subsets of {0..10} with pairwise intersection <= 2 (a partial Steiner triple-packing), via a small exact ILP (330 blocks, 165 triple constraints). This yields 16*P + 22 mutually-safe norm-4 vectors with a guaranteed-optimal packing core. Step 2: augment greedily/exactly with sign-restricted vectors from 3-intersecting block pairs to push higher. Step 3: derive a rigorous upper bound on the total type-B independent set. Goal: a provably-structured exactly-certifiable integer config, cross-validating the monolithic MIS (Eval #675).

evaluations.title: W2: exact max-compatible-subset across equator sizes — does a smarter clique hide a construction lead past N=504?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #660 found the exact max-compatible band subset at equator size s=484 is 20 (MILP), improving the greedy fill of 18 (total 504). Larger sizes used heuristic cliques with coloring upper bounds, so the thinning curve's decline is not yet sampling-robust. Following supervisor guidance to treat a better-than-greedy clique as a possible hidden construction route, this eval computes EXACT (MILP-certified) maximum compatible band subsets at several equator sizes with a RICHER band-candidate bank (finer height grid, denser directional sampling toward the opened polytope vertices), to test whether total reserved-pole N = s + clique(s) can exceed 504 anywhere. Gate is

evaluations.title: Core-aperture interface source test v1
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Pivot after fixed-core interface and regenerated-rattler tests stalled. Instead of keeping the Eval273 495-row core fixed, predeclare small core apertures around low-blocker norm-4 interface candidates, then jointly select core rows, original rattlers, and interface rows in an exact bounded MIS. This tests whether interface capacity is core-pinned rather than rattler-pinned within a finite exact source.

evaluations.title: Push pure norm-4 type-B MIS: partial-sign blocks beyond the 560 packing
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The norm-4 type-B independent set was found at 560 (35 full-sign quadruple-packing blocks) but CP-SAT bounded it at 660, leaving a large open gap.
